apiDocs.title: drop API
apiDocs.subtitle: Programmatic file uploads for drop.leod.me — get a short, shareable link from a single curl call.

intro.heading: Introduction
intro.p1: drop API is the public HTTP interface of yui-drop. It lets scripts, command-line tools, and other applications upload files programmatically and receive a short, shareable code in return.
intro.envelopeLabel: All responses use a uniform envelope:
intro.signupLabel: API keys are not self-served. See

auth.heading: Authentication
auth.p1: All /api/v1/* endpoints require a Bearer token in the Authorization header:
auth.p2: Tokens follow the format yd_ + 8-character public ID + _ + 32-character secret. The first 11 characters appear in admin lists and audit logs; the full plaintext is shown exactly once at issuance and is never recoverable.
auth.errorScope: 403 — Insufficient scope (key lacks upload or read)

upload.title: Simple upload — files up to 10 MiB
upload.description: Upload a small file using multipart/form-data. The response contains a 5-8 character pickup code, a direct download URL, and a short link. Files larger than the server's simple-upload cap should use the multipart endpoints below.
upload.paramFile: Multipart field containing the file body
upload.paramExpireValue: Numeric value for the expiry unit (≥ 1, default 1)
upload.paramExpireStyle: Expiry unit (default day; see expire_style values)

multipartInit.title: Multipart upload — step 1: initialise
multipartInit.description: Large files use the R2 multipart presigned URL protocol. The client first calls init to receive an upload_id, then iterates over parts_total to request presigned PUT URLs, uploads each part directly to R2, and finally calls complete.

multipartSign.title: Multipart upload — step 2: sign one part
multipartSign.description: Call once per part (1 through parts_total) to receive a presigned PUT URL for that part. The client then uploads the byte range directly to R2 and records the returned ETag header.

multipartComplete.title: Multipart upload — step 3: complete
multipartComplete.description: Call once all parts have been uploaded. The server forwards the part manifest to R2 to assemble the final object, validates the resulting size (> 5% deviation fails), creates the share, and returns a response identical to simple upload.
multipartComplete.paramParts: Full part list (number + ETag); length must equal parts_total

multipartAbort.title: Multipart upload — abort
multipartAbort.description: Discard an in-progress multipart session. Uploaded parts are reclaimed by R2 and the session row is deleted.

listShares.title: List shares created by this key
listShares.description: Paginated query of all shares uploaded with the current API key. status defaults to active; pass expired or all to widen the result set.

getShare.title: Fetch a single share
getShare.description: Returns the same shape as a list item. Only shares created by the current key are returned — others 404 (to prevent enumeration with someone else's key).

clients.heading: Client libraries
clients.p1: Clients chunk files locally and upload each part directly to R2 — the yui-drop server only mints presigned URLs. Three implementation paths cover most use cases:
clients.curlBody: Suitable for one-off uploads from a shell. Roughly 30 lines, no dependencies beyond curl and jq. See scripts/yui-drop-upload.sh in the repository.
clients.pythonBody: Suitable for scripts and automation. The reference implementation at scripts/yui-drop-upload.py uses requests and a thread pool to upload parts concurrently.
clients.uppyBody: For browser and Node clients, @uppy/aws-s3-multipart maps onto this API directly. Implement the four lifecycle methods (createMultipartUpload, signPart, completeMultipartUpload, abortMultipartUpload) by proxying to /api/v1/upload/* and Uppy handles chunking, concurrency, and retries automatically.

expireStyles.heading: expire_style values
expireStyles.footnote: expire_value is N in the table; it must be ≥ 1 (ignored for forever).
expireStyles.count: expires after N downloads (expired_count is decremented)

errors.heading: Error codes
errors.notFound: Share or upload session does not exist or is not owned by this key

quota.heading: Quotas
quota.p1: Each API key has three independent quotas, all of which the administrator can override at issuance time. Defaults:
quota.quotaDailyBytes: quota_daily_bytes: 5 GiB / day — cumulative bytes within a UTC day
quota.quotaPerMinute: quota_per_minute: 30 / minute — call rate (reserved; not yet enforced)
quota.p2: quota_daily_bytes = 0 means unlimited. Usage is rolled up daily in api_key_usage; simple uploads are recorded on success and multipart uploads are recorded on complete.

requestKey.heading: Request a key
requestKey.p1: drop API does not currently offer self-service signup. To request a key for your scripts or to integrate yui-drop into your project, contact:
requestKey.p2: Each key can be issued with an independent note, scopes, quotas, and expiry. The plaintext key is shown exactly once at issuance — save it immediately to your password manager.
